lines.en: Another day means another chance to fall into an uncovered manhole and be eaten by the secret alligators in the catacombs of Kumon-mi.
That probably isn’t the most constructive thought I’ve had first thing in the morning lately, but at least it’s an interesting one.
Being eaten by an animal would be a good way to go. And no one would be able to get mad at me for it since the animal would be too easy to blame.
And also, it would give those I care the most about a fun story when they’re recollecting their youth fifty years from now to grandchildren who will have escaped the shade of my family tree.
I’ve been talking to myself a lot lately.
I don’t mean to, but it’s a thing I keep doing and I don’t understand why.

It’s never anything interesting. Mostly just quick utterances of vague fatalisms like “I want to die” or “I fucking hate myself,” but they always make me feel off because I’m the only one around to hear them.
And I already know those things. I gain nothing from watching them fall from the horse’s mouth. I am the horse. Complete with oversized penis and everything.
I don’t know.
I hope something interesting happens today.
I hope I get to see an alligator.
My phone rings.
I press the button that bridges the gap between where I am and where I’m never meant to be.
: Good friggin’ mornin’, Sensei! Or, as they say in the states, “Good friggin’ mornin’!”
: Well that’s certainly a joke that doesn’t translate very well.
: I don’t get it. But there’s tons’a stuff I don’t get, so I’m willin’ to overlook that in favor of gettin’ the talk-ball rollin’!
: The...what?
: Idunno, I’m just sayin’ stuff at this point. How ya been lately? Wiener still floppin’ around all floppy-like and stuff?
: I...guess so?
: Great! Cause that means you can bring it on over here for a day of action and adventure, Miku-style!
: New Miku style? Or old Miku style? Because those are very different things and require very different levels of participation on my end.
: Mmm...old Miku style? I ain’t tryin’ to put it in my mouth today. Just wanna see your face and stuff.
: It’s been a while, hasn’t it?
: Yeah. Life is kind of terrible. Sorry I haven’t been keeping in touch.
: Nah, I get it. I’ve got too much energy for even Makoto sometimes and she’s been dealin’ with me forever. But a little dose every now and then ain’t all that bad, right?
: Oh, and before ya go misunderstandin’ that last part — that ain’t, uhh...whaddy’a call them things again? Metal...forks?
: ...Metaphors?

: Yeah! That “dose” thing ain’t a metal fork for medicine. I’ll have ya know I’m still goin’ strong without that stuff! Therapy’s been okay, though. Talkin’s still hard. And I haven’t even gotten to the tough stuff yet.
: Oh! And my grade’s are doin’ kinda okay now! And...let’s see...what else is goin’ on...hmm...
: Swimming! Yeah! The club’s been-
: Are you just...going to recap me on everything that’s been happening in your life the last couple months? Right now?
: Is now a bad time? Should I call back later?
: I mean...if it’s going to be long, I can just come see you.
: You’re actually okay with that? Kinda figured you were gonna shoot me down.
: We ain’t hung out in months and you ain’t been in any rush tryin’ to put an end to that. Which is perfectly fine! I know things are tough right now.
: We can meet. It’s not like I’ve been avoiding you on purpose or anything. That’s just...sort of a side-effect of all of this.
: Awesome! Can ya come to the park, then? I’m havin’ a picnic thingy with Io and Uta and I’m sure they’d be happy to see you too!
: Three girls at once ain’t too much, is it?
: Three girls at once is actually a major fantasy of mine.
: That a sex joke?
: Yeah, that was a sex joke.
: Heck yeah! I understand those now. Ain’t sure how well that’s gonna work in public, though. Think there are laws against that kinda thing.
: Either way! Get your butt over here ASAP! I’ll let the others know you’re comin’.
: Sure. It’s the park near the school, right?
: Yeah, the one where Otoha’s always playin’ guitar and stuff.
: Is she there right now?
: Mmm...no. Don’t see her. Just some old guy with a weird coat and- oh. Oh.
: Ya know, maybe that public stuff is legal after all?
: I’m on my way. Stay away from the old guy, please.
: Yeah, I’m just gonna...I’m gonna jog around the track while waitin’ for the others to show up.
: Bye, Sensei! See ya soon!
I hang up the phone and pull myself out of bed. But while I’m getting dressed, my mind strays from alligators and catacombs and lands on something brighter.
Maybe Miku is precisely the type of girl who can share some of her light with me — in the good way. Not the Yasu way.
Or the Yasu way if she thinks she’s ready. But...not in public.
There are laws against that sort of thing.
When I make it to the park, it finally dawns on me how beautiful the weather is today.
I was so distracted on the way here by the idea that I might be biting off more than I can chew that I wound up forgetting how nice it is to be rid of the summer.
That is until a familiar scent makes me yearn for the snow.
But I forget that again when my heart is thawed by a surprisingly wholesome sight.
: Well, if it ain’t Captain Sorrow in the flesh!
: Hi, Sensei! Long time no see! If you’re not counting the part where Uta and I broke into your house and tried to kidnap you.
: Hahah...yeaaah...That’s a thing that happened, alright...
: I can’t say I’m fond of my new nickname, but hey. To all three of you. Sorry for turning into a hermit.
: Ain’t nothin’ to apologize for, Sensei. I’d probably be go into hidin’ too if my niece started sayin’ stuff that made her sound like a serial killer.
: ‘Specially cause I ain’t got a niece and that would make stuff extra scary. But I get it.
: Ami is not a serial killer. She’s just...kind of-
: Yeah, yeah, yeah. Let’s not talk about weird nieces right now. Let’s shoot for something different instead! Like the best way to cook steak. Or weird pictures we might keep in our phones!
: Io! Shh! No!
: Weird pictures? You tryin’ to confess to somethin’ right now, Io? What’choo keepin’ in there?

: Oh, you know. The same kind of stuff everybody else does. I just figured this might be a good chance to clear up any misunderstandings before our imaginations start to fester and kill us from the inside out.
: Yeah, I’d rather not talk about what I keep in my phone.
: You don’t say.
: Does everybody keep weird stuff in their phone but me? This another one of those adult things I ain’t learned about yet?
: Everything okay, Uta? You look upset.
: I’m...uhh...confused. That’s all.
: Sensei, do you maybe want to talk to Uta for a minute while Miku and I...go over...uhh...
: ...there?
: Hah...
: Now wait just one second, Io. I didn’t ask Sensei if he wanted to come all the way over here just so he could have some alone time with your roomie.
: And I know that for sure ‘cause I got my own roomie who always wants alone time with Sensei and that’s just rude when we’ve got a whole group of people doin’...group stuff.
: I agree! Group stuff it is! Talking about what we have in our phones is super personal and private anyway! What we don’t know won’t hurt us! Right, Sensei?!
: Uhh...right. Exactly.
: Well, now that all that weird stuff is outta the way, how we gonna do this? Under the table? On top of the table? I gotta know where to put the pizza.
: Wait, what are we talking about now?
: Another misunderstanding. Please ignore everything Miku says that sounds even remotely suggestive and just continue to be your normal, cynical self.
: Now that is a task I can handle.
: Well, if we’re gonna be law abidin’ citizens and all that, what can we do? Cause Sensei ain’t the type to enjoy any kinda socially acceptable physical activities.
: Boy am I glad I was just told to ignore everything even remotely suggestive.
: Miku, why don’t you continue filling me in on everything else that’s been going on? You know, in a way that can’t possibly lead to anyone hearing anything they don’t want to hear?
: How the heck am I supposed to be keepin’ track of what other people wanna hear when I don’t even know what I wanna hear?! I ain’t some kinda event organizer!
: Heck, I didn’t even know I was supposed to bring anything to this picnic and I’m the one who kinda organized it! I clearly ain’t cut out for this!
: It’s cool, Miku. Uta and I brought more than enough for all of us. Plus, we had a big breakfast earlier, so neither one of us is that hungry.
: I ate three bowls of cereal. I am not proud of myself. But I also didn’t know we were even having a picnic until we were on the way here, so...
: She probably doesn’t remember that we’re going to the movies tonight either. Uta and I both have mid-shifts, though, so we can’t stay for super long.
: She’s right. Totally forgot about that until right now.
: See?
: I’m what most people like to call a “lost cause.”
: Why put together a picnic in the first place? That’s far too passive of an activity for someone like you who seems to exist for the sole purpose of just...running around and yelling.
: I gotta eat too, Sensei. All that runnin’ and screaming requires some serious fuel and my battery ain’t gonna recharge itself.
: Plus, everybody’s been lookin’ so darn sad lately that I felt like I needed to do somethin’. And gettin’ you outta the house as well was a crazy bonus that even I didn’t expect.
: Yeah. Not gonna lie, after you gave us that speech in school, I was pretty confident you were going to go right back home and allow yourself to be chained up or something.
: We were all worried about that. Which is probably why we’ve all seemed so “down” lately.
: Uta in particular has taken your absence really harshly. I haven’t seen her this miserable since they stopped selling the umeboshi onigiri at Lawson — the place where I work.
: Halloween is over, Io. You don’t have to pretend to work at Lawson anymore.
: Once a Lawson, always a Lawson. That’s what Mr. Lawson always says.
: Miku- and you two as well, I’m sorry. Okay? It’s not like I wanted to make any of you upset. And while I’m flattered that you’re all this down because of me, you need to snap out of it.

: Like, look at what’s become of Miku. She’s trying to organize events now and is clearly horrible at it. Her words, not mine. But also my words. Even I know everyone is supposed to bring something to a picnic.
: And yet you have shown up empty-handed. Curious.
: It ain’t just that, though, Sensei. I’ve been kinda messed up too. I’ve really missed you.
: You’ve been more than just a teacher for a long darn time. And havin’ you stuck in your house is kinda like havin’ a friend move away. So I’m tryin’ to bring some of the fun back into life.
: You have any idea how many times I’ve wanted to call ya since you disappeared? Your name in my phone’s like, the last thing I look at every night.
: Been dreamin’ about you too, but I don’t think I can talk about those with my other friends present.
: Come to think of it, I’m pretty sure Uta has as well. Because I’ve definitely been hearing “Sensei...Sensei!” in the middle of the night a lot lately.
: Hahaha! Not me! I don’t have any dreams at all! Ever!
: How are you not embarrassed saying things like that out loud, Miku? I’m not even talking to Uta right now and I can already tell she’s internally screaming.
: (Fuck!)
: What’s there to be embarrassed about? If somebody’s gonna shame me for lovin’ my friends, they ain’t somebody I wanna hang out with in the first place.
: The thing I want the most right now is for you to get back to normal. So if I’ve gotta start organizin’ picnics to do that, I’m gonna.
: Sure. Except for the part where we’ve never had a picnic before and this isn’t really normal either.
: The picnic ain’t the important part, it’s bein’ together that is. So I’ve been tryin’ to spend time with everybody lately to remind ‘em all that this is just temporary.
: You’re gonna get better, Sensei. And maybe it won’t ever be “normal” again if whatever ya lost was really that important to ya. But still...we’ve gotta do somethin’.
: And that somethin’ may as well be fun.
I take a seat at the picnic table with all three of the girls and force myself to eat a slice of pizza despite barely having an appetite for over a month.
And while the conversation that picks up once the introductory phase of our rendezvous comes to an end is simpler, something still feels off.
It could very well be the fact that I just haven’t spent much time with any of these girls since before the incident, but that’s probably just wishful thinking.
It only makes sense that there are some things happening behind the scenes that I don’t know about. Miku’s living proof of that.
But it seems that finding out what’s going on with Uta and Io will have to wait as the two of them bid Miku and me farewell once the sun begins to set, leaving us alone once more.
For the first time in a while.
: Did you know that some people do it in the butt? Crazy, right?
: And it’s like no time has passed at all...
: Huh? What do you mean?
: Nothing. Just narrating my thoughts again.
: You do that often?
: Not really. But I’ve been talking to myself a lot more than normal lately, so I guess that’s a thing.
: Weird. Makoto’s been doin’ that too. Figured it was just stress or somethin’.
: It might be. There’s certainly been no shortage of that since my sadness-coma.
: Wanna talk about it? I’ve learned a thing or two about therapy lately. And if that kinda thing works for somebody like me-

: Maybe some other time, but not because I don’t trust you. It’s because I don’t want to put an end to this...haphazardly organized soiree meant to serve as a re-introduction to a less sorrowful reality.
: I’ve got no frickin’ clue what any of that just meant, but okay. Long as you’re happy.
: I’m not.
: Then what the heck were all of those big words for?!
: I’m just commending you for trying. It’s really nice of you to go to all this effort just to try and pick up the slack I’ve created by...semi-vanishing.
: Oh...yeah.
: It’s been hard. All of this stuff. And I ain’t just sayin’ that cause I’ve had to go back to usin’ my own fingers.
: The thing is...I really like you. Lots of us do. But since I haven’t been able to get to you, I’ve just been tryin’ to pick everybody else up instead.
: Makoto’s...fine, I think? Which is weird. But she also just had some crazy trauma with her dad recently that might’a helped her deal with stuff like people vanishin’ a little better, though.
: Sana’s been weird, though. Io’s been worse than normal. Uta’s cryin’ a lot. Futaba seems stressed. Kirin’s kinda...I don’t know. Let’s just say she’s weird too. But Ayane’s got it the worst.
: She cries in the shower after swim club so nobody will notice, but I do. I always do.
: You...watch Ayane shower often?
: Body goals, Sensei. Body goals.
: Ayane’s got the kinda figure girls like me can only dream of. Had no idea I’d stumble upon her havin’ a secret breakdown in there. But she won’t even talk to me about it since we ain’t close.
: Ayane doesn’t like talking about things like that with anyone. She’s like me. More of a...bottle it up type of person.
: I get it. You know I do. But we’re all gonna wind up miserable if we keep doin’ that to ourselves. Which is why I just want us all to...get back to where we were at the start of the year.
: Back when...
: When...
: Wait...what? Weren’t you absent at the start of the year? How does that...nah, I’ve gotta be.....
: A-Anyway! If things are ever gonna be fun again, me and you are-
: You and I.
: You and I are gonna have to cross this...bridge or somethin’ together! Which means continuin’ to explore and continuin’ to enjoy each other’s company! Both sexually and not sexually!
: And...which one of those things do you want most right now, Miku?
: Both! I am very conflicted and very excited to see you again!
: Which means...
: Which means?
: Which means there is only one place the two of us can go...to kill both birds with a rock.
: Not how that phrase goes, Miku.
: Things have changed here on the outside while you’ve been gone, Sensei. You don’t know how we talk anymore.
: Miku, just tell me where we’re going.
: To the promised land, Sensei.
